title: A Little Flour, Always Enough
story: The Jar That Never Ran Out
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
A widow had a little boy
and hardly any bread.
The jar was almost empty now,
the last meal, so she said.

[Chorus]
Share, little one, though it feels small,
and give with all your heart.
For God can make a little lot;
that’s where His blessings start.

[Verse 2]
Elijah asked, “Please bake for me,”
and though her heart was scared,
she gave her last, and then the jar
stayed full because she shared.

[Chorus]

[Verse 3]
Now close your eyes, my little one,
your tummy’s full tonight.
Heavenly Father fills our home
and holds you till it’s light.

[Chorus]
mood: Kitchen music. A slow, kneading sway under the voice, rounded and patient, like a mother’s hands working the last bit of dough. Each chorus lifts a little, the way the jar keeps on giving. By the final verse the sway slows and drops lower, warm and full, until the room feels fed and quiet.
